sourceLanguage: English source excerpts and English explanation shared by both routes. No new translation or fallback.

sourceComparisons.source: Mosbach et al., sections 4–5, Figures 2, 4 and 8
sourceComparisons.preserved: A near-trivial training loss distinguishes an unfitted classifier from two fitted runs with different development predictions. Lower-layer gradient observations do not prove a universal saturated-tanh explanation.
sourceComparisons.example: Balanced binary loss log(2); prescribed fitted/dev predictions; constructed head gradient 0.7310585748 versus lower gradient 6.02729617e-9. Examples are labelled synthetic.

sourceComparisons.source: Zhang et al., section 4 and Algorithm 1; Mosbach et al., sections 5–6
sourceComparisons.preserved: Historical BERTAdam omission, moment estimates and corrected update, fixed-current-moment ratio, epsilon/weight-decay caveats, empirical failure rate scoped to the authors' 50-seed BERT-Large experiment.
sourceComparisons.example: g=2, beta1=.9, beta2=.999, alpha=.001 gives raw update .00316227766 and corrected update .001; ratio at t=10 is about 6.528, not monotone linear warmup.

sourceComparisons.source: Zhang et al., section 5 and BERT branch of run_glue.py lines 736–764 at 0aa4f4e117ee4422f7cb9355158203e01d6730db
sourceComparisons.preserved: Architecture and lower pretrained weights retained; parameter-type initialization; pooler reset separately; both retained/reset blocks remain trainable; optimizer created after reset.
sourceComparisons.example: Three small blocks: count zero leaves all blocks unchanged, count one preserves lower two, LayerNorm becomes one/zero; invalid counts rejected. This is not a full BERT run.

sourceComparisons.source: Zhang et al., section 6; Mosbach et al., section 6
sourceComparisons.preserved: Epoch/update distinction, warmup trajectory, checkpoint candidate count, eight seeds for budget selection versus twenty for reporting; longer training is an experimental choice rather than a universal recipe.
sourceComparisons.example: 1000 examples, batch 32, three epochs -> 96 retained-partial-batch updates or 93 drop-last; 2400 -> 225; 20 epochs on 1000 -> 640.

sourceComparisons.source: Zhang et al., section 7 and Table 2
sourceComparisons.preserved: Additional labelled MNLI supervision and cost; encoder transfer with correctly shaped target head/new optimizer; target-task results and deviations, not a universal superiority claim.
sourceComparisons.example: Supplied four-dimensional intermediate encoder, three-class intermediate head and two-class target head; one target update changes the copied target encoder but not the original checkpoint.

sourceComparisons.source: Mosbach et al., sections 4–6 and original repository Figure 1; Zhang et al., experimental methodology
sourceComparisons.preserved: Optimization failures and residual generalization variation; all-run distributions; legitimate validation-based stopping distinguished from survivor-only reporting; development protocol not ranked directly against another study's test halves.
sourceComparisons.example: Scores .50,.51,.70,.72 have mean .6075; dropping two failures reports .71 while hiding a 50% failure rate.

sourceComparisons.source: Hu et al., section 5.5 and Table 4, distinguished from section 7/Table 5
sourceComparisons.preserved: Reported GPT-3 175B full/4.7M/37.7M adaptation results remain task-specific; separate experimental adapter counts do not establish universal quality/speed/memory.
sourceComparisons.example: 4.7M FP16 parameters are about 9.4 decimal MB; 18M are about 36 MB; rank 256 factors of a 4096-square projection are one eighth of its full parameter count.

sourceDiscrepancies: Zhang et al. CoLA Re-init differs between source Tables 1 and 2. The chapter explicitly follows Table 2 (64.2 ± 1.6) and does not silently mix it with Table 1 (63.9 ± 1.9). Both original PDF pages were visually inspected.
explanationReview.reasoning: All fourteen published CPU fences executed in order; added independent checks and negative controls verify gradients, reset boundaries, transfer shapes and memory arithmetic. These small examples do not reproduce a BERT/GLUE study.
explanationReview.style: Full chapter reread against no-ai-slop plus local academic-writing qualifications. Preserve quoted source prose, necessary terminology, derivations, examples and caveats; no generated diagram replaces a source illustration.
explanationReview.notClaimed: No full-model training, GPU QLoRA, GLUE benchmark reproduction, universal hyperparameter rule or comprehensive catalogue of every PEFT algorithm.

negative_controls: zero block count does not select all blocks
cpu.scope: Small CPU algebra/gradient examples, not full-model tuning or GPU QLoRA
